questions.question: Which of these commonly causes traffic crashes?

options.text: Driving above the speed limit or driving too fast for conditions.
Getting enough rest and staying alert.
Looking ahead and focusing on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving above the speed limit or driving too fast for conditions.
questions.explanation: Driving too fast is a common cause of crashes. Always drive at or below the speed limit and adjust your speed for road conditions.

questions.question: Your reaction time is slower after:

options.text: Drinking alcohol.
Sleeping.
Working hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drinking alcohol.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reflexes and reaction time. It reduces your vision and makes you less alert. As you drink more, your judgment gets worse and your driving skills decrease. You will have trouble judging distances, speeds, and other vehicles.

questions.question: When driving in work zones, you should:

options.text: Follow the driver in front of you closely.
Pass the driver in front of you as soon as possible.
Keep a safe distance and do not follow too closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a safe distance and do not follow too closely.
questions.explanation: In work zones, keep a safe distance from barriers, trucks, equipment, workers, and other vehicles. Stay farther back than usual and do not follow too closely.

questions.question: Which of these can affect your ability to drive?

options.text: Tranquilizers, marijuana, and sedatives.
Cough syrups and cold tablets with codeine or antihistamines.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Many drugs can impair your driving. These include tranquilizers, sedatives, marijuana, cough syrups, cold tablets, and allergy medicines. Some of these contain alcohol, codeine, or antihistamines that affect driving.

questions.question: What should you do with loose objects in your vehicle?

options.text: Place them on the floor near the driver's seat.
Secure them so they do not become hazards.
Place them on the dashboard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure them so they do not become hazards.
questions.explanation: Loose objects can hurt people if you stop suddenly or crash. Objects on the floor can roll under the brake pedal and prevent you from stopping.

questions.question: Before changing lanes or passing, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Signal your intention to other drivers.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes or moving your vehicle left or right. Check your mirrors and turn your head to look at your blind spot before moving.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Sharp turn to the right ahead.
Sharp left and right turns ahead.
Winding road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Winding road ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you of a winding road ahead. Slow down and adjust your speed.

questions.question: If a railroad crossing has lowered gates and flashing lights, you should:

options.text: Drive around the gates if you don't see a train.
Stop behind the gates, wait until the tracks are clear, then proceed when the gates lift.
Slow down and drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop behind the gates, wait until the tracks are clear, then proceed when the gates lift.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when signs, warning devices, or flaggers indicate a train. It is illegal to drive around lowered gates.

questions.question: When driving on gravel or dirt roads:

options.text: Your tires grip better than on pavement.
Your tires have less grip than on pavement, so slow down.
Visibility is better than on pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires have less grip than on pavement, so slow down.
questions.explanation: Gravel and dirt roads have less traction than paved roads. You must slow down. It takes longer to stop and you can skid more easily when turning.

questions.question: Speeding too much:

options.text: Saves time and gets you there faster.
Helps you avoid obstacles.
Increases the risk of serious injury and death.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the risk of serious injury and death.
questions.explanation: Excessive speed is a leading cause of crashes. It does not save time and often leads to dangerous decisions.

questions.question: If there is no crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian can see you before you drive.
Drive carefully around the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
questions.explanation: You must always give pedestrians the right-of-way, even if there is no marked crosswalk.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Four lanes of traffic ahead.
Divided highway ahead.
Two-way traffic ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about dangers ahead. This sign warns that you are leaving a one-way highway and entering a two-way highway.

questions.question: What is the only way to remove alcohol from your body?

options.text: Drink strong coffee.
Time.
Take a cold shower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Time.
questions.explanation: Only time will remove alcohol from your body. Drinking coffee, eating, or taking a shower will not speed this up.

questions.question: If you are getting tired while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and rest or let another person drive.
Drink something with caffeine.
Open a window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest or let another person drive.
questions.explanation: To stay safe, take a break every hour on long trips. Share driving with another person so you can rest while they drive.

questions.question: Why should you not make sudden stops in front of large trucks and buses?

options.text: Small vehicle drivers cannot see large trucks and buses well in their mirrors.
Large trucks and buses need longer distances to stop because of their size and weight.
Large trucks and buses travel faster than small vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks and buses need longer distances to stop because of their size and weight.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles take longer to stop than smaller vehicles. A sudden stop in front of them is dangerous because the driver may not be able to stop in time.

questions.question: Is it permitted to drive while taking medication that affects your driving?

options.text: Never.
Yes, if you don't feel drowsy.
Yes, if a doctor prescribed it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive under the influence of any substance that affects your driving ability. This includes alcohol, prescription drugs, over-the-counter drugs, and illegal drugs.

questions.question: A school bus ahead of you has red lights flashing. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and go when you think the children have exited.
Slow to 25 mph and pass carefully.
Stop and stay stopped while the red lights are flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and stay stopped while the red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights, you must stop and stay stopped until the lights stop flashing. Exception: You do not need to stop if the bus is on the opposite side of a divided highway.

questions.question: When a school bus on your side of the road has red lights flashing, you must:

options.text: Slow to no more than 10 mph.
Stop until the lights stop flashing.
Change lanes and pass carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: Flashing lights and a stop arm on a school bus mean students are loading or unloading. You cannot pass until the lights stop flashing and the arm is pulled in. Never pass a school bus that is picking up or dropping off students.

questions.question: If you see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead, what should you do?

options.text: Keep going. You have the right-of-way.
Wait for the pedestrians to cross.
Pull to the right and go around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the pedestrians to cross.
questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk. Wait until they have fully crossed before driving.

questions.question: When you see a stopped school bus with its stop arm extended and lights flashing, you should:

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait.
Honk your horn and pass on the left side.
Keep driving when most kids have exited the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait.
questions.explanation: When a school bus is stopped with its stop arm extended and lights flashing, come to a complete stop. Stay stopped until the arm is pulled in and the lights turn off.

questions.question: If you drive faster than other vehicles on a two-lane road and pass cars often, you will:

options.text: Get to your destination much faster and safer.
Increase your chances of a collision.
Help reduce traffic congestion.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your chances of a collision.
questions.explanation: Avoid passing other vehicles on two-lane roads. Each time you pass another vehicle, your risk of a collision goes up.

questions.question: Changing lanes is best done:

options.text: Quickly and often.
When a car is in your blind spot.
Slowly and carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly and carefully.
questions.explanation: Always change lanes slowly and carefully. Only change lanes when you need to. Every lane change increases the risk of an accident.

questions.question: If you feel drowsy while driving, you should:

options.text: Try to fight the drowsiness.
Take a break.
Take caffeine pills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a break.
questions.explanation: If you feel tired while driving, pull over at a rest stop or service area. Take a nap, stretch, or have someone else drive. Do not rely on caffeine pills or energy drinks. They are not a real solution and may make your driving more dangerous.

questions.question: If you see animals near the road while driving:

options.text: Speed up to scare them away.
Slow down and drive with caution.
Quickly swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and drive with caution.
questions.explanation: Slow down and drive carefully if animals are near the road. They may suddenly run into traffic or change direction. Animals often travel in groups, so more animals may be hidden nearby.

questions.question: If your vehicle breaks down:

options.text: Signal and move to the slow lane.
Stop in your lane and turn on hazard lights.
Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down on a highway, get it off the road and away from traffic if possible. Turn on your hazard lights so other drivers can see you are having trouble.
